learn.title: Learn
learn.subtitle: Simple explainers, a bilingual glossary, quizzes and teacher packs.
learn.glossaryBody: Polar terms in English and Hindi.
learn.quizBody: Test yourself on an item. Every question links to its source.
learn.teacherPackBody: A printable one-page activity sheet with glossary terms and discussion questions.
learn.hindiReview: Hindi meanings are drafts awaiting expert review.
learn.noQuizzes: No quizzes yet — they appear once items have text.
learn.l1p1: The polar regions are the areas around Earth's North and South Poles — the Arctic and Antarctica. Scientists also study the Himalaya, often called the “third pole” because it holds so much ice.
learn.l1p2: These cold places matter to everyone: their ice, oceans and weather are connected to the rest of the planet. Research stations let scientists observe them year after year.
learn.l1p3: In DhruvGyani you can read reports, look at data and photos, and ask for any item to be explained at your level.
learn.l2p1: Sea ice is frozen seawater that floats on the ocean. It grows in the cold of winter and shrinks in summer.
learn.l2p2: Land ice — glaciers and the great ice sheets of Antarctica and Greenland — is built from snow that has piled up over thousands of years. Where an ice sheet flows out over the sea it forms a floating ice shelf.
learn.l2p3: Floating ice is already in the water, so when sea ice melts the sea level barely changes. When land ice melts or slides into the sea, the sea level rises.
learn.l3p1: Earth's axis is tilted. For part of the year each pole leans towards the Sun, and for part of the year it leans away.
learn.l3p2: Near the poles this means the Sun does not set for weeks or months in summer — polar day, the “midnight sun” — and does not rise in winter, which is polar night.
learn.l3p3: Station teams plan around it: most field work happens in the light of summer, and the long dark winter is the hardest season to work in.
learn.l3more: See the sun at each station now
learn.l4p1: An ice sheet is built from layers of old snow. Drilling out a long cylinder of ice, called an ice core, lets scientists read those layers like the pages of a book.
learn.l4p2: Tiny bubbles trapped in the ice hold air from the time the snow fell, so ice cores show how the atmosphere and the temperature changed in the past.
learn.l4p3: Satellites have measured the extent of sea ice since 1979, and expeditions such as MOSAiC measure the ice, the ocean and the air from the surface.
learn.l5p1: India runs research stations in all three cold regions. Maitri and Bharati are in Antarctica, Himadri is at Ny-Ålesund in the Arctic, and Himansh is in the Himalaya.
learn.l5p2: The work is led by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
learn.l5p3: The Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica takes scientists and supplies to the stations; the 46th expedition has been announced.
learn.l6t: Why the poles matter to everyone
learn.l6p1: Bright ice and snow reflect sunlight back to space and help keep the planet cool. When the ice melts, the darker ocean or land beneath absorbs more heat.
learn.l6p2: Melting land ice raises the sea level around the world, including along India's long coastline.
learn.l6p3: The cold polar oceans also help drive the currents that move heat around the planet. That is why changes at the poles are watched so closely.

about.title: About DhruvGyani
about.body1: DhruvGyani (ध्रुव ज्ञानी — “one who knows the poles”) is a prototype outreach, knowledge repository and media dissemination portal for the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences, built for Smart India Hackathon 2026 problem statement SIH26063.
about.body2: It brings expedition reports, datasets, publications, photos, videos and institutional activities into one searchable library, linked by expedition. Its Content Studio helps staff draft website articles and social posts in English and Hindi, with every claim cited, checked and approved by a person.
about.p2: Fit NCPOR, don't replace it — link to existing portals, offer RSS and embeds.
about.disclaimer: This is a hackathon prototype and is not an official NCPOR website. Archive content comes from the public sources credited on each item.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.intro: DhruvGyani aims to be usable by everyone, including people who use screen readers, keyboards, magnifiers or high-contrast settings.
accessibility.targetBody: We target WCAG 2.1 Level AA, the baseline of the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW 3.0).
accessibility.f1: English and Hindi interface, with correct language attributes.
accessibility.f2: Text-size controls (A−, A, A+) and a high-contrast mode, in light and dark themes.
accessibility.f3: Full keyboard navigation, a skip-to-content link and visible focus indicators.
accessibility.f4: Alternative text for images and transcripts for videos.
accessibility.f5: Reduced motion is respected when your system requests it.
accessibility.l1: Some linked external NCPOR documents (PDFs) may not be fully accessible; we link to them as provided.
accessibility.l2: The map is visual; the same station information is available as a list beside it.
accessibility.l3: Hindi translations of some content are drafts awaiting expert review.
accessibility.contactBody: If you find a barrier, please tell us through NCPOR's official contact channels and mention the page address.
accessibility.tryItBody: Language, theme, contrast and text size.
